apples_jimmy.summary: The account has made credible specific calls, including on Claude 4’s timing and capabilities, an xAI o1-style model, and upcoming OpenAI products. Their record is mixed, with notable misses on Gobi, GPT-5, GPT-4.5, and Meta’s model weights; most evaluated claims concern OpenAI. Some posts relay information that was already public, so individual claims are best read skeptically.

aibattle_.summary: The account is generally dependable on concrete, checkable artifact reports, including arena codenames, console references, and model-version sightings; its strongest records include xAI, Alibaba, and Zhipu, while results on Google and OpenAI are solid but less consistent. Speculative release or reveal claims warrant more caution: notable misses include Nightwhisper, GPT-4.5 Turbo, DeepSeek V4 GA, and GLM-5-Code. A substantial share of claims were already public when posted, and several recent model and artifact claims remain pending.

haider1.summary: Mainly an aggregator and commentator on OpenAI and Anthropic; much of the output relays reports, company statements, or rumors already public. The account has made strong calls on OpenAI milestones and release timing, as well as Kimi K3, but launch-timing claims are mixed, with misses on Gemini 3.5 Pro, Astra 6.1, and Claude Fable 5.5; its settled record is strongest on OpenAI, while evidence on other labs is thinner and mixed. Recent claims about November releases from Anthropic, DeepSeek, OpenAI, and Moonshot remain pending.

tetsuoai.summary: A commentator focused on xAI whose posts mostly relay news that was already public. The account has a supported short-term Grok release-timing call, but missed detailed feature and pricing-roadmap claims; a claim about monthly foundation-model releases remains pending. The small record offers limited support for treating the account as an original leak source.

phill__1.summary: The account is strongest on concrete model and release details, with supported calls on Llama 3.1 405B benchmarks, Qwen’s reasoning model with vision, and Gemini 2.0 Flash. The record is small and includes partial as well as mostly accurate calls; some posts relay already-public news, and release timing may be conditional.

iruletheworldmo.summary: The account has made some notable near-term timing calls, including GPT-6’s September window and Astra’s September 3 release, but its overall record is weak, with OpenAI its comparatively strongest area among the major labs it covers. They have missed specific dates, specs, and benchmark claims—including on GPT-5.3, Sonnet 5, and an April GPT-6—and some recorded hits were already public. Recent claims about further Fable and SSI news, a November frontier-model release window, and a Google model held in reserve remain pending.

ns123abc.summary: The account mostly relays already-public reporting, and its settled record is mixed: its calls about Meta hiring and an xAI release were accurate, while its Anthropic Fable timing claim was mostly accurate. It made a notable false claim about Trump’s proposed public-partnership framing; recent claims remain unverified.

chrisgpt.summary: The account has made credible OpenAI product and timing calls, including the GPT-6 August target, and its record is strongest on OpenAI; its small set of xAI calls has also landed, while Anthropic results are mixed. It has missed a Meta model-release prediction and an Anthropic Fable 5.5 claim; many posts relay already-public reporting, and several recent Anthropic claims remain pending.

yuchenj_uw.summary: A commentator rather than a dedicated leaker, the account has shown useful OpenAI signal on GPT-5 routing and open-model timing and capabilities, and has made some accurate release-date calls. The settled record is mixed, with misses on specific release predictions and an unsupported claim about employee bonuses; many claims relay information that is already public, and recent claims remain unverified.

alexeheath.summary: The account’s reported claims have held up well so far, including calls on OpenAI ads and Altman’s return talks and Meta’s H1 2026 model plans; no settled misses are recorded. The sample remains limited, some claims were already public, and the claim about Anthropic’s appearance at Microsoft’s CEO summit is still pending.

synthwavedd.summary: The account’s strongest record is on OpenAI, with well-supported calls on Astra’s rollout timing, though some other speculative OpenAI launch claims have missed. Their Anthropic record is mixed despite a successful Opus 5 launch-window call, and their Google record is weak; a notable share of posts relay information that is already public, while claims about unreleased models and internal codenames can be difficult to verify.

chetaslua.summary: The account combines hands-on model testing with relays of others’ reporting; its settled record is stronger on Google and Zhipu claims. Launch calls such as GPT-5.5 and Gemini Spark have largely held up, while OpenAI claims are less consistent and Anthropic is a weak spot, with IPO, AGI, and Codex claims among the misses. Treat sweeping or longer-range claims cautiously, and note that several recent claims remain pending.

tokengremlin.summary: The account has a reasonably solid but imperfect settled record, driven mainly by OpenAI calls, with notable successes on GPT-6 Astra and Sol timing and rollout signals. Their smaller Anthropic record is mixed, and they have missed several near-term launch predictions, including for Fable 5.5 and GPT-6 Luna, as well as a later GPT-6.1 Astra timing claim; some calls are qualified or inferential. A notable share of posts relay information already public or summarize same-day announcements, while several recent development and product-behavior claims remain pending.

scaling01.summary: The account is a fast-moving commentator and relayer rather than a demonstrated insider; some calls concern information already public, limiting the evidence of lead time. Their settled record includes accurate near-term release calls for OpenAI and Moonshot, as well as misses on Google's training-data claim and SpaceX's 10T-model claim. Broader claims about internal capabilities, model scale, and timelines remain pending and should be treated cautiously.

dseetharaman.summary: The account's settled record is strongest on OpenAI, with supported Reuters reporting on restructuring tensions and agent-related incidents. The record is narrow and mostly reflects published Reuters reporting, offering limited evidence about advance warning or reliability beyond OpenAI.

btibor91.summary: A prolific reverse engineer of the ChatGPT and Claude apps, the account has a strong settled record, particularly on Anthropic, where its calls have been consistently accurate. Its code-level finds have included the ChatGPT image editor, the Aura browser codename, and Claude Code on the web, though code references are not guarantees; some posts relay already-public news. Misses include claims about Sora, GPT-5.2-Codex-Max, and a $100 ChatGPT Pro Lite tier, while many recent findings remain pending.

m1astra.summary: An anonymous app-teardown account focused mainly on OpenAI and Anthropic, with a stronger record on Anthropic and good calls on Claude voice and memory features, as well as OpenAI’s Astra and GPT-Bidi-1. They often identify near-term product work from app or site changes, but also relay already-public material and have missed by over-reading assets or strings, including claims about Sora features and ChatGPT subscription plans. Recent claims remain unsettled.

techdevnotes.summary: The account tracks xAI product, app, and API traces, though many claims are already public and some plans are inferred from those traces. They have made successful calls on OpenAI and Grok features, but settled xAI claims skew toward misses, including launch timing and extrapolations about Grok features or model characteristics; a UI or API trace alone does not confirm a launch.

aibreakfast.summary: The account is an AI-news aggregator with a mixed settled record; its strongest listed call was that OpenAI would reveal the GPT-4V API and autonomous agents. Its speculative calls about Gobi, GPT-4.5 Turbo, and o3’s launch-day timing and capabilities missed, so forward-looking claims warrant more caution than announcement-related coverage; the settled sample is limited.

xfreeze.summary: The account is an xAI-focused aggregator, and many posts relay public statements or news rather than offer independently verifiable forecasts. Its limited settled record is favorable, with confirmed and partly correct calls and no recorded misses; recent claims about xAI engineering work and Grok Build features remain pending and unverified.

testingcatalog.summary: The account’s app-code and build-reference findings have often held up, particularly on Anthropic, Google, and Meta; many OpenAI claims have also been credible, though some receive only partial support. Many posts relay already-public news, and speculative forward-looking feature claims can miss, as with the Claude iOS redesign and Perplexity Computer claims. Several recent feature claims remain unverified.

bindureddy.summary: The account often relays circulating rumors or public expectations rather than first-hand leaks, and many credited calls were already public. OpenAI is its strongest area, with several successful launch and model calls, plus an isolated Anthropic hit; results are weaker on Google and DeepSeek, and the record offers no evidence of strength on xAI. Gemini claims about parameters, relative capability, benchmarks, pricing, and latency have often been unreliable, while several recent claims remain unresolved.

ai_for_success.summary: An aggregator that mostly relays news, rumors, and official teasers, much of which is already public or reported the same day. Its claims about Gemini Omni, Gemini Spark, and Gemini 3.2 Flash have generally held up, but predictive launch-timing calls are less dependable: a claim that a new version of Jules was close to launching was false. A recent claim about an Anthropic model remains pending.

shiringhaffary.summary: A Bloomberg AI reporter, the account has a strong record on OpenAI funding, restructuring and products, with well-supported reports including Operator, the SoftBank-led funding round and the employee secondary sale. Their settled record shows no outright misses, though some calls are rated mostly true rather than fully true, so reported plans or terms may not match the final outcome exactly.

wongmjane.summary: The account has a strong settled record for identifying in-development features, with successful calls across OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, and Meta; notable examples include ChatGPT file support, Bard features, and Advanced Voice on the web. Some posts concern features that were already public, and the Cloudflare–Stripe integration claim was a miss. Recent claims about a Claude avatar creator, Meta Pay for Muse, and two Instinct features remain unresolved.

daniel_mac8.summary: The account's overall record is mixed, with a somewhat stronger record on OpenAI than Anthropic. Near-term timing has been a relative strength: GPT-6 Astra's launch day was called exactly, GPT-5.5's timing was broadly right, and Opus 5 was forecast about eight days ahead; longer-range GPT-6 forecasts were repeatedly too early, and the account made false Sonnet 5 launch calls. A substantial share of claims was already public, so originality is a caveat.

kimmonismus.summary: The account is an aggregator that often relays other leakers and public sightings, so many claims are already public by the time they post; their claims are generally specific. Stronger calls have involved OpenAI releases and access, as well as Grok 4.6, while Anthropic calls have been mixed: model timing and access calls have fared well, but the claim that Anthropic was ending Haiku was false. Claims about Anthropic’s Fable 5.5, Obsidian 3 and Mythos 5.5, and Meta’s Muse Spark 1.4 remain unverified.

flowersslop.summary: The account has a mixed OpenAI track record: claims about GPT-5.5’s existence and agent improvements, Images v2’s unusually high-resolution generation, and GPT-6 model and lineup plans have been rated positively. Several near-term release, voice-mode, and AVM predictions have failed, so they appear more useful for specific model or product leads than release timing; recent claims remain unsettled.

kateclarktweets.summary: The account is strongest on explicit financing, valuation, and deal scoops, especially around OpenAI and also Anthropic, with well-supported calls on investor participation and transactions. The supplied record has no outright misses, though some calls are only mostly true and may be imprecise on figures or details; the evidence here concerns business and deal reporting, not model-release leaks.

tomwarren.summary: The account is a Microsoft/Xbox reporter whose concrete claims have generally held up, especially on Microsoft; the settled record has no outright misses, though one claim was only partly accurate. Their record is strongest on Microsoft/Xbox, the Meta sample is limited, and an Xbox disc-to-digital internal-testing claim remains unconfirmed.

imjustnewatai.summary: A high-volume anonymous account with a mixed record: it correctly identified GPT-4.5 as in development and has made accurate OpenAI timing calls, including for o4, ChatGPT-5 and GPT-6. But elaborate, confident claims about GPT-5, DeepSeek R2 and Grok 5 have failed, and quantitative details such as context windows and prices remain unreliable; Google looks like a relative bright spot on limited evidence, while results on other labs are weaker, and some posts relay already-public news.

vraserx.summary: Mainly an enthusiast amplifier rather than an original source: many posts restate official announcements or other people’s claims, sometimes after the fact. Some broad calls have been supported, including a June window for GPT-5.6, Google Omni, a Codex iOS app, GPT-6 as a new pretraining run, and a possible full-duplex voice mode; exact timing and detailed product or capability rumors have often missed, including the June 11 GPT-5.6 date and Astra. Recent claims remain pending.

amir.summary: The account has a strong, well-supported record on business, funding, and infrastructure scoops, including OpenAI–Amazon financing, compute, and commerce discussions; Microsoft’s OpenAI partnership; and Nvidia’s Blackwell delay. No settled misses are listed, but several recent claims remain pending and are not yet evidence of accuracy.

anissagardizy8.summary: A WSJ infrastructure reporter with a strong record on compute, chips, and funding scoops, including the Blackwell delay, xAI’s planned 100,000-H100 cluster, and Anthropic and Amazon/OpenAI funding news. The settled record has no outright misses, though some calls are only partly confirmed; coverage spans several major AI labs, with especially strong results on OpenAI.

teortaxestex.summary: A DeepSeek- and China-focused commentator, with a sparse record that makes reliability difficult to assess. Concrete calls are mixed: a mostly correct identification of Ox Alpha as GLM-5.3 Flash, alongside false claims that Astra weights had leaked and that DeepSeek would release DSH 0.2 with V4.1 Pro that week.

pankajkumar_dev.summary: An aggregator-style account that posts frequent, detail-heavy leak threads about OpenAI, Anthropic and Google. OpenAI and Anthropic development and timing claims have often held up, though both have notable misses; specific Google claims have been less reliable, including the false Snow Bunny report. Much of the account’s material appears to relay public reporting, so codenames, benchmarks, pricing and model attributions warrant caution; recent claims about Gemini 4 Carbon-H and other unreleased models remain unverified.

mark_k.summary: The account makes frequent, specific short-horizon launch calls, with accurate calls including xAI’s Grok 4.5 and OpenAI’s Astra, but its record is mixed across both labs and includes notable misses on launch timing and product details. Many claims were already public when posted, which limits their value as early signals.

markgurman.summary: The account has a strong record on Apple strategy and AI plans, including reporting on Google’s role in a Siri overhaul, an AI-powered search tool, and Siri features under development. Settled calls on OpenAI and Meta have also been accurate, though coverage there is limited; the account missed a specific claim about iOS 27 Siri behavior, and some other calls were only partly accurate. Detailed claims about upcoming Apple products remain pending, and some posts reiterate earlier reporting or information that was already public.

steph_palazzolo.summary: The account, an Information AI Agenda reporter, has a strong track record on OpenAI and Anthropic, especially on business, funding, and policy; claims are generally right in substance, though some specifics can be partial or change. A notable miss on OpenAI’s planned Sora launch in ChatGPT means product plans warrant extra caution, and several recent claims remain pending. Many posts promote same-day Information stories, so lead time is often short.

erinkwoo.summary: A tech reporter (formerly The Information, now WSJ) covering Google and OpenAI, the account has a strong but still limited record on specific claims, including Google’s Pentagon agreement and Gemini developments, and OpenAI’s Astra preview. Of 13 settled claims, 12 were accurate and one was partly accurate, with no misses; some reports concern internal details that can be difficult to verify independently, and a recent OpenAI claim remains pending.

legit_api.summary: The account has a generally solid record on pre-release model details and benchmark claims, with notable calls involving Gemini, GPT-4.5, and Grok; its record is strongest on Google claims and also good on OpenAI and xAI. They are less dependable on precise launch timing and product or API feature predictions, and some claims concern information that was already public. Recent claims about Anthropic’s Fable 5.5 and its VoxelBench performance remain pending.

andrewcurran_.summary: The account is mainly an aggregator, often relaying reporting that is already public rather than offering original leaks. Its calls about Gemini, GPT-Astra’s clearance, GPT-5.6’s release status, GPT-6 Sol, and Spud have generally held up, but specific claims have missed, including the Anthropic private-equity venture and Astra’s cyber access; recent claims about internal models and a continual-learning breakthrough remain unresolved.

smokeawayyy.summary: The account makes terse model-and-date calls, sometimes with specific release times. Their limited OpenAI record includes a correct GPT-5 date call and partly right calls about ChatGPT memory and an April release bundle, but misses on GPT-5o and o3-mini timing; many claims repeat information already public, so their predictions are most informative when they add novel specifics.

deredleritt3r.summary: The account mostly relays already-public reporting and OpenAI materials, with no verified successful calls in the settled record. Its settled claims that OpenAI had achieved AGI, would separate from Microsoft (including an alleged agreement over that separation), would declare AGI in 2025, and would soon release an Olympiad-winning model were false; recent claims about GPT-5.6 Sol Pro and unreleased internal models and their benchmark performance remain unresolved.

kyliebytes.summary: The account's tracked claims have generally held up, including reports on Anthropic's planned Gulf investment and API-access decision, Meta's hiring and compensation offers, and OpenAI researchers joining Meta. Some posts relay information already public, coverage remains limited, and recent claims are unresolved.
